workspaceGate.environment: GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04, Node 24.15.0, pnpm 10.34.5 (run 31402467593, head 8b63846)

deferredChannels.reason: No Apple Developer ID or Windows signing certificate has been procured, so no notarized DMG, signed MSI, deb or AppImage exists. The native release policy still requires a verified upgrade from an older signed installer before any stable native artifact ships.
The Tauri updater channel depends on signed native artifacts and is deferred with them.
Packages are version-locked and pack cleanly, but publication requires the maintainer's npm account and GitHub Actions OIDC on the canonical tag workflow.

notes: INCOMPLETE RECORD. This file carries machine evidence only. `releaseOwner` and `licenceCompliance` are absent because both are human attestations that no automation may sign, so `node scripts/validate-public-release-approval.mjs --tag v1.2.0` fails closed until a person adds them. Their required shape is in release/acceptance/README.md; the 1.1.0 record is a filled example.

1.2.0 is additive over 1.1.0. The REST surface, OpenAPI document, SDK, nineteen-tool workflow registry, five-tool terminal session registry, CLI and .marketingovo bundle format are unchanged, so no existing integration breaks.

What it adds: the six-language console (English, Azerbaijani, German, Russian, Dutch, Spanish) with a picker in the command bar and in Settings; roughly 1,990 interface strings moved into a typed catalog under apps/dashboard/src/i18n where tsc refuses a locale missing a key and a unit test refuses one whose {placeholder} markers drifted; the hand-made pixel sprite set with its provenance ledger; and the vendored Departure Mono web font under the SIL Open Font License, recorded in NOTICE with the licence text beside the font.

The terminal-ui-pixel-assets channel that 1.1.0 declared deferred has shipped in this release and is therefore no longer listed. The console no longer falls back to inline SVG stand-ins or the platform monospace stack.
All seven gates were observed against tree 8b63846, which is this repository's main tip, rather than carried forward from the 1.1.0 record.

workspaceGate was observed on Linux CI rather than on the maintainer's host. `pnpm check` cannot complete on Windows: packages/credentials' native-broker test spawns a POSIX-shebang script directly and fails with EFTYPE, and five other suites assert chmod modes, symlinks, executability, or delete a temp directory SQLite still holds open. The same command passes on ubuntu-24.04 in the run named above. The other six gates were observed locally on Windows and also passed in that CI run.

A dependency advisory was fixed rather than waived while preparing this release: nanoid 3.3.16, reached transitively through vite and vitest, carried a HIGH advisory that failed pnpm audit:dependencies closed. The lockfile now resolves 3.3.18.

The repository had no .gitattributes, so a contributor whose git uses core.autocrlf=true received a CRLF working tree, and three gates that read files line by line failed on it: validate:skills could not find command frontmatter, audit:dependencies could not find the lockfile's packages and snapshots sections, and validate:plugins reported every generated agent surface as stale against byte-identical output. CI runs on Linux and never observed it. Text files are now checked out with LF on every platform.

Three version pins did not move with the bump at first and were caught by the gates rather than by review: the Codex bundle's .codex-plugin/plugin.json, which is hand-maintained rather than produced by pnpm plugins:generate; the CLI packable assertion in scripts/npm-release-policy.test.mjs, which wrote the version as the regex /marketingovo@1\.1\.0/u where escaped dots hide it from a search for the version, and which now reads the version from package.json; and the Tauri crate version in Cargo.toml, which would have shipped a 1.2.0 bundle whose launcher reported 1.1.0.

One CI job was not reproduced locally: `cargo check` for packages/credential-broker-native and apps/desktop/src-tauri. Rust is not installed on the maintainer's host, so that gate rests on the CI matrix rather than on a local observation, as it did for 1.1.0.

CodeQL reports open alerts on this tree. They are not introduced by the changes in this release — main carried 39 open alerts before it, and the alerts attributed to the merged pull request sit in files whose only change was a version string. They are unreviewed rather than accepted, and triaging them is outstanding work, not evidence recorded here.
